To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the cost per bit metric is becoming increasingly less relevant, (ii) the DRAM chip micro-architecture is ripe for a major overhaul, and (iii)a few key architectural modifications can lead to significant energy and reliability gains.

(i) selective bit-line activation can reduce the energy consumption of a DRAM chip by 6X with a 4% area penalty, (ii) single subarray access can reduce the dynamic and background energy consumption of a chip by 6-7X, and (iii)single subarray access can lead to a 54% performance improvement on average by reducing queuing delay, and (iv) checksums can reduce energy and storage overhead of RAID-like fault tolerance by 4X
